## Environment fingerprint

- Framework `objectstack-ai/objectstack` main @ **`8e3d4a54`**, the same tree and build as record-A-P0 (09:07–09:10Z). Tier 1 pins at this sha all green (3,403 tests, 0 failed; record-A-P0). The upgrade items' own automated.ref (Tier 1, supporting — every clause here was also driven live on the 18.3.0 file): activation-ledger-package-key.dogfood 8✓ + 1 skip (memory driver, `it.skipIf`), activation-ledger-packageless-index 19✓, activation-ledger-backfill 16✓; stored-reference-package-column.dogfood 7✓, automation-stored-reference-package-column.dogfood 5✓; stored-references.integration 12✓, stored-package-references.literal-namespace 13✓.
- **18.3.0 golden database.** The #32093 18.3.0 project (`qa183`) copied and extended per #32093: three flows (a 60 s schedule, a record-after-create approval routed to queue `qa183_reviewers`, an autolaunched one), one permission set, one sharing rule, queue `qa183_reviewers`, `requires` gaining `approvals`, and two packages `com.example.qaa` (qa_a) and `com.example.qab` (qa_b) each declaring queue `qa_desk`. **18.3.0's own `objectstack dev`** (scheduled work on) wrote the rows through its own endpoints: member, grant, queue member, a pending approval with a paused run, three activation toggles, an environment flow saved by PUT, three dispatch rows. Then by SQL, the #32093 plants: `package_id` NULL on the ledger rows, the environment ledger row, a managed sharing rule, an email-template overlay, a binding suggestion, a flow credential and a 73-day-old dispatch key; WAL checkpoint. Golden sha256: v183.db `d46bbea5…b349e`, v183.telemetry.db `8dec0a12…f2312`. Every clause ran on a fresh copy of the golden pair.
- **Subject run.** The project copy's `@objectstack/*` dependencies symlinked to the 8e3d4a54 tree's packages, and its `objectstack` binary pointed at the tree's `packages/cli/bin/run.js`. Boots `dev --no-watch --no-compile`, scheduled work off; `migrate plan` / `apply` with `NODE_ENV=development` so the telemetry sibling is composed. Ports 41230–41245.
- Timestamps (UTC): one runner, 09:11–10:00 shared with the four cli P0 items (setup ≈30 min incl. the 18.3.0 config, boot and plants; test ≈55 min across both). A first migrate-stored-references pass copied the telemetry sibling without its `-wal`; it was discarded and every clause re-run on checkpointed copies.

## Scope

Selector `release-18.4.0-w1-upgrade` at 8e3d4a54 → 3 items, all rev 1: platform-core.activation-ledger-package-key-upgrade · platform-core.stored-reference-package-backfill-upgrade · cli.migrate-stored-references.

## Derived item verdicts

| PARTIAL (1) | platform-core.stored-reference-package-backfill-upgrade (A0 sub-legs R11 `connector_package` and R13 `rule_package` blocked(fixture): the app declares no connector instance and no assignment rule, so there is no one-holder name to plant; every other table's leg passed) |
| PASS (2) | platform-core.activation-ledger-package-key-upgrade · cli.migrate-stored-references |

## Round 1 FAIL re-drive (#32093 clause 5, activation ledger)

Fixed. On a copy carrying two package-less rows for one flow: boot 1 refuses to build the package-less index, naming the probe SQL and `os migrate duplicates`, and refuses to bind either row, naming both row ids; boot 2 with nothing deleted refuses again and leaves the rows byte-identical with no index. After one row is deleted and the server restarted, the index is built and the remaining row binds to its one package.

## Fails — reproduction rule and disposition

None.

## Off-clause probes (rule 8)

Per-item minutes and doors are in the probe log (record-A-UPG-clauses-1.md). No product defect found.

Observed and not carded (low): the managed sharing-rule row planted by SQL in the #32093 shape makes every boot log an ERROR saying the declared rule of the same name is not in force — loud, correct, but it repeats on every boot.

## Parked-on #32908

Fixture gaps: a connector instance and an assignment rule in the 18.3.0 upgrade fixture (R11 / R13 legs). Stored-references R3: a binding suggestion planted by SQL for a set that is not `isDefault` is pruned by the boot by design, so R3 was scored on a separate leg (the same app with `isDefault: true`, where 18.3.0 wrote the suggestion itself and the subject bound it); the fixture recipe should say so.

Per-item checklist-accuracy notes follow.

**platform-core.stored-reference-package-backfill-upgrade**
- fixtures.requires[0] says to plant "a sys_audience_binding_suggestion row naming a set one package holds (R3)" by SQL. A pending suggestion for a set no package declares `isDefault` is PRUNED by the boot's syncAudienceBindingSuggestions (packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/suggested-audience-bindings.ts, "A pending row whose declaration is gone … is pruned") — measured: the SQL-planted qa_abs_1 row vanished on boot 1 of u1. So R3 needs the set declared `isDefault: true`; this run did that on…
- The SQL-planted managed sys_sharing_rule row (QA run #32093's shape) collides with the declared rule of the same name: every subject boot logs ERROR "[sharing-rule] declared sharing rule 'qa183_share_notes' arrives over a stored sys_sharing_rule row of the same name, so the declared rule is NOT in force …". The backfill still binds the row; the fixture should plant a managed row under a name the package declares only as a stored copy, or accept the line.

**cli.migrate-stored-references**
- Runner note (no product impact): a first pass on copies m1/m2 took the telemetry sibling without its -wal (the upgraded copy had not been checkpointed), so those siblings were the 18.3.0 shape; bind's composed boot then added the flow_package column there (additive DDL, no row values changed). The pass was discarded and every clause above re-run on checkpointed copies m3/m4. A copy recipe for this item should say "checkpoint (or copy the -wal) after the upgrade boots".
